summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with Type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis s/p gastric pacer, hypertension, and GERD was admitted for acute nausea and vomiting. She presented with dehydration, elevated blood pressure, and sinus tachycardia, but no signs of pancreatitis or bleeding. She was treated with IV fluids, antiemetics including Zofran, Compazine, and Ativan, and continued on metoclopramide via her port. Her insulin regimen was maintained with Lantus and sliding scale Humalog. Over the hospital stay, her symptoms improved, vital signs normalized, and she advanced to tolerating oral intake with toast and ginger ale. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue her gastroparesis diet, medications, and follow up with gastroenterology to evaluate her gastric pacer.
